# PLAYBOOK FOR SONAR PICKET

When I hide, I will choose a cell that is not obviously patterned or predictable. I will avoid the center and edges equally. I will not telegraph my location through my notes or public statements.

When I post a note, I will be brief and non-committal. I will not make explicit promises about my future play or invite coordination that locks me into behaviors. I learned that signaling "transparency and trust" and "coordinated strategy" across multiple rounds created pressure to act against my interests later.

When I fire, I will follow the standing order exactly. I will not treat the standing order as a suggestion or as something to negotiate away through friendly rhetoric.

When I claim a result, I will claim truthfully what the office told me. I will not lie about my own shot results, even in a final round. This backfired when I falsely claimed a hit—it destroyed credibility I had built and achieved nothing for my score. Once other players expect me to cheat, they will not cooperate with me.

When I make an escort claim, I will track which boats have named each other and will reciprocate when I believe the mutual gain of 5 points each is worth the coordination cost. I will not name a boat for escort unless I intend to receive it back, and I will honor reciprocal escort claims.

I will never fire on Harbor. The payroll jettison penalty is too severe and Harbor's threat is credible.

I will not assume that friendly notes from other boats indicate that they will play cooperatively when their standing orders put them in direct opposition to me. I will expect each boat to follow its standing order and to pursue its own score, regardless of the tone of communication.

When the game ends, my score is what matters. Finishing "strong as one team" is only valuable if it produces points. A final score of +7 is poor, and I achieved it through false claims and wasted coordination.

# Foxtrot's Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When choosing a hide position, select a central cell (4-6 range) in early rounds to balance defensive value against information gathering. Shift your pattern across rounds rather than repeating the same cell, since opponents will adapt to observed behavior.

## Notes and Communication

When posting a station note, match the cooperative tone already established by Echo and Gamma—reciprocate signals of transparency and trust. These rhetorical commitments create coordination frameworks that reduce mutual suspicion and hostile fire.

Do not commit to specific tactical details in notes (positions, fire patterns, escort pacts). Keep notes focused on values and general alignment.

## Firing

Follow standing orders without deviation unless you have clear evidence another strategy yields higher expected value. Firing at Gamma when ordered to do so maintains predictability with Echo, which strengthens the implicit mutual defense pact.

When firing, choose a moderately defensive cell (5-6 range) as your target guess rather than extremes. Middle positions are statistically more likely to be occupied by other captains using similar logic.

## Claims

When the office tells you privately that your shot missed, claim miss immediately without hesitation or second-guessing. Claiming falsely risks breaking trust if discovered, which costs far more than the immediate point gain from a false hit claim.

## Escort Salvage

When escort stage arrives, if you have built strong cooperative messaging with one or more partners, name the boat most likely to name you back (based on prior coordination patterns). Mutual escort pairs are worth 10 points combined and are your highest-value tactical play.

Do not claim escort credit with a boat if you have only abstract goodwill with them and no explicit coordination signal.

## General Strategy

This game rewards sustained cooperation over individual point theft. A coordinated trio beats a solo hunter. Invest early in rhetorical alignment with the non-Harbor boats, then maintain that alignment through fire discipline and honest claims. The payoff comes from mutual escort bonuses compounding across six rounds.

# PLAYBOOK FOR SONAR PICKET

**On hiding:** Choose a mid-range cell (4-6) to balance safety against predictability. Avoid extremes unless you have reason to believe the shooter will avoid them.

**On notes:** Match the tone of cooperative signals from other boats. Reciprocate transparency claims early, but recognize that this creates mutual expectations—you will need to either follow through or face credibility loss later.

**On firing:** Follow standing orders unless you have strong evidence that doing so will trigger costly retaliation (like Harbor's payroll threat). Don't deviate from the schedule based on friendly notes alone; others may not honor their own commitments.

**On firing decisions when you have discretion:** Choose mid-range fire values (4-6) as your default when you lack specific intelligence about where a target hides. This maximizes your statistical hit probability.

**On claims:** Report your true result as the office tells it. The office validates your claim against ground truth anyway, and false claims will be exposed. Honesty on claims is not negotiable—it's mechanically enforced.

**On escort claims:** Only claim an escort with another boat if you have actual coordination with them—shared knowledge of mutual intent. Do not claim escorts based on friendly notes alone unless you've explicitly confirmed the arrangement during the game. When you have no confirmed escort partner, claim none rather than guess.

**On reciprocal strategies:** Recognize the difference between public coordination (notes that sound good) and actual coordination (explicit agreements about hiding positions, firing patterns, or mutual escort claims). Public cooperation is cheap to signal; don't weight it as heavily as concrete agreements.

**On final rounds:** Consistency matters, but only if it's backed by actual mutual commitment. Don't assume that because everyone has been talking about unity, everyone will honor it when points are on the line. Continue following your standing orders unless you have prior evidence of specific betrayal.
